title: What is an upstander, and how can you be one?
examples: How can I help someone being bullied?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Even one upstander can change everything

explain.say: Imagine you see someone being picked on in the playground. What do you do? Look at the left side of the board. A bystander, which means someone standing by, sees it but watches, laughs or walks away.

explain.say: Now look at the right side. An upstander also sees it, but does something safe to help. You do not need to be a superhero. Small actions count. Which side would you like to be on?

explain.say: Here is how. First, do not join in: no laughing, filming or sharing. Then, if it feels safe, say something: hey, that is not okay. Can you say that in a strong, calm voice?

explain.say: And always tell a trusted adult, like a teacher or parent. Telling is helping, not snitching. Amazing! Wow fact: research found that when a classmate steps in, bullying often stops within about ten seconds.

faq.a: An upstander is someone who sees unkindness or bullying and does something safe to help, like speaking up, helping the person leave or telling an adult.
A bystander sees bullying happen but does not help. Watching or laughing can make the bully feel they have an audience.

faq.q: What can I say to stop bullying?
faq.a: Short and calm works best: Hey, stop. That is not okay. Or: Leave them alone. Only speak up if it feels safe; otherwise, get an adult.
asks: Tell me about the Say something

faq.a: No. Snitching is trying to get someone in trouble. Telling is trying to get someone out of trouble or harm. Telling an adult about bullying is helping.
asks: Tell me about the Tell an adult

faq.q: What if I am scared to speak up?
faq.a: That is okay. You can still be an upstander by not joining in, being kind to the person later, and telling an adult quietly.
asks: I am too scared to help

facts: A 2001 Canadian playground study by Hawkins, Pepler and Craig found that when peers stepped in, bullying stopped within 10 seconds more than half the time.
Pink Shirt Day began in Canada in 2007 when two students handed out pink shirts to support a boy who was bullied for wearing pink.
